t: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Homeland Security of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate an assessment of the efficacy of the Coast Guard’s Standard Operational Planning Process with respect to annual mission performance measures.

fable.w: The section requires the Comptroller General (GAO, a federal entity) to submit an assessment to congressional committees. The tempting reading is that a formal report or submission requirement is participatory, but both the sender and the recipients are inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted or given any role in a federal decision.
fable.s: the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Homeland Security of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate an assessment

qwen_block.w: This section requires the Comptroller General (a federal official) to submit a report to congressional committees. Congress and its committees are considered inside the federal government. Therefore, this is an intra-governmental reporting requirement, not participation by outside parties.
qwen_block.s: the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Homeland Security of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate an assessment

opus.w: This section only requires the Comptroller General to send an assessment to congressional committees. Everyone involved is inside the federal government. A report to Congress looks procedural, but it never brings in the public, states or experts, so it is not participation. There is no comment period, hearing, outside consultation or right to sue.
opus.s: the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Homeland Security of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate an assessment
opus.b: The tempting reading is that a formal assessment submitted to congressional committees counts as a procedural step involving other parties. It doesn't. The Comptroller General (GAO), the Coast Guard and the House and Senate committees are all inside the federal government, and no outside party is consulted or given a role in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Comptroller General (a federal official) to submit a report to congressional committees. Congress is considered inside the federal government. There is no requirement to consult or coordinate with any outside parties such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities. Therefore, this does not constitute participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Homeland Security of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate an assessment
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that because the Comptroller General is assessing a process, there is some form of consultation or participation involved. However, the text only mandates a report to Congress. Congress is inside the federal government, and the Comptroller General is a federal officer. There is no requirement to consult with states, tribes, the public, or other outside entities.
